boon.Alertness: You are never *not* paying attention. While everyone else is asking, "What was that?" You are already turning to face the threat. You pay attention to everything... to the point of being called "paranoid" more than once.
boon.Alternate Identity: You have a second life. There's an address that receives your mail. There are neighbors who could describe you to a sketch artist without a second thought. It all stands up to scrutiny because it is all real. It's a lot of work, but worth it for the benefits it grants.
boon.Always Connected: You are the one who never says, "I don't have any bars!" There is always a signal and you are connected to it. While the rest of them are wandering around with their phones in the air, you've already sent the file.
boon.Ambidextrous: Most people have a dominant hand. For you, whichever hand is free is the dominant one.
boon.Animal Rapport: Dogs cross the street to greet you. The cat that no one gets to pet sits in your lap. Your friends describe you as a "Disney Princess," and they aren't wrong. You can't communicate with them and you can't tell them what to do. Animals just trust you on sight.
boon.Common Sense: Most people don't realize they did something stupid until it's too late. The little voice in the back of your head says, "I wouldn't do that. It's a bad idea." And you listen. Most of the time. When you do something stupid, you can't say nobody warned you.
boon.Compact Frame: When other people have to squeeze into a tight space, you just walk on through. Vents, the space behind the cabinet, the crowd other people have to muscle their way through are non-issues for you. It works the other way, too - you can easily disappear in a crowd.
boon.Concentration: Once you start something, you will finish it. You studied for finals in a bar during a GWAR concert and aced them. Gunfire, explosions, a demolition crew tearing the building down around you - none of it is a distraction.
boon.Danger Sense: It's quiet... Too quiet. Something is wrong. You don't know what it is, you just know. Something warns you when you are in danger.
boon.Displaced Echoes: Mockingbirds, magpies and you. You hear a car alarm, a chainsaw, a snippet of a song and can imitate it perfectly. It's not an impression, but you mimic the sound precisely.
boon.Distinctive Features: There is something about you that is visibly different. You might have something non-human in the family tree or you might have Bette Davis eyes. Or a tail that helps you balance, gills, fur, markings that can't be mistaken for a birthmark. They are unusual, but useful.
boon.Double-Jointed: You saw a man fold himself into an acrylic box on The Gong Show and decided you wanted to do the same thing. Now, if you can get your head through it, the rest of you will follow.
boon.Duelist: You picked a weapon and learned everything about it. It is no longer a tool - it is a part of you. The guy across from you has trained. You have specialized.
boon.Eidetic Memory: Everyone else's memories fade and slowly rearrange themselves as time passes. Yours do not. You don't remember things, you access the files. The page is there in front of you. The license plate is on the car at the stoplight in your mind.
boon.Enchanting Voice: You could read the phone book and people would lean in to listen. The velvet tones of your voice rival the Sirens or Orpheus. Something in your voice makes people decide you are worth listening to. You can't switch it off.
boon.Encyclopedic Knowledge: You read something about this once. It was in a psychology journal. "Why did I read it? It seemed interesting." You devour information and it sticks with you. It doesn't matter where the information came from, you are almost always right.
boon.Extra Limbs: Most humans have two arms and two legs. Some have less, which brings the average down. You are trying to bring the average back up. You have more limbs than a "normal" human. Whether it is more arms, legs, tentacles, they are yours. They work and your body has never been confused about their function. Complex tasks are easier, but finding a suit that fits is hard.
boon.Eye for the Opening: You don't hit harder than anyone else. You don't have to. You see the opportunity - when their guard dips, they are shifting their weight and are vulnerable or when their attention flickers to something behind you - and you seize that moment.
boon.Eye for the Strange: No one noticed, but when you walk into the room, you feel it. Something isn't natural and you can spot it - the shadows are too deep, there is a cold spot following a conversation. You can sense the supernatural.
boon.Familiar: You have someone... or something that has chosen you. A black cat followed you home. A book started talking to you one day. A spirit attached itself to you and never explained why. Whatever it is, it is competent, loyal and willing to go places you can't.
boon.Feign Death: Your body is a biological machine and you have learned to shut the whole machine down... temporarily. You appear dead in every way that matters.
boon.Higher Purpose: You have been chosen for a specific purpose. By what? You don't know. It might be fate, a debt, an elder god. Whatever it is - it has a vested interest in seeing that your story ends after you achieve this goal. When you go, it will mean something.
boon.Innate Compass: You don't get lost. Ever. North is that way. It's just a fact you have access to, the same way you know which way is up. You always know roughly where you are, even without a map. That doesn't stop people from handing you the map, though.
boon.Iron Grip: Your hand is a vise. If you have a grip on it - it stays in your hand.
boon.Iron Stomach: Gas station sushi. The leftovers with no clear date on them. Water out of something that isn't a tap. Whatever it is, you imbibe it, and then you are fine. Anyone who shared it with you - not so much.
boon.Iron Will: Your mind is your own, and the door only opens from the inside. People who try to read you come away with nothing - no tells, no tics, no flicker behind the eyes to work with. People who try to push you find out that pushing was the only thing they brought.
boon.Jack of all Trades: And a master of none. Being a jack of all trades is often better than mastery of a couple skills. You've picked up things here and there. None of it is remarkable, but you know how to do a little of everything and that matters more often.
boon.Lie Detector: It's never the words. Anyone can rehearse a story until it reads as true. It's the half-second hesitation, the glance away, the detail that is a little too on the nose. Everybody tells you when they are lying - you just know how to listen to what they are really saying.
boon.Light Sleeper: You have never slept through anything in your life. Most nights, it's a curse. You wake up before the sound is gone. You are awake and ready to go.
boon.Lightning Calculator: You don't do the math. You don't have to - you just know the answer. The odds, how much fuel remains, the required angle to land the shot - the numbers are there. You are moving while everyone else is reaching for the calculator app on their phone.
boon.Natural Linguist: Some people have a knack for mathematics. Others have an ear for music. You have an innate understanding of languages. Within a few minutes of exposure to a language, you begin to understand it - where the verbs belong, which sounds are doing the heavy lifting, the patterns unique to the language. Give it a day, and you can survive.
boon.Never Off Balance: You've fallen (or been knocked down) enough times to have an opinion about it. You lose your footing and you are already recovering.
boon.Quick Study: One quick read through is usually all it takes. People don't like it when you pick something up over an afternoon that they spent the last five years mastering.
boon.Restful Trance: Three hours of meditation and you feel like a million bucks. You don't dream, toss and turn, or drift off to sleep - you turn your brain off and flip it back on just as easily. No one who sees it thinks it looks restful, but they don't know what they are missing.
boon.Special Movement: You move in a way most people can't - crawling up a wall, walking over snow without a trace, swinging on grappling hooks. Whatever the method, physics filed an objection and no one listened.
boon.Special Weapons: You have one specific piece of hardware that nobody should be walking around with, and you know exactly how it works. Where it came from is your business. Whether the paperwork exists is nobody's business. It is yours, it is the only one you get, and it does something a normal weapon cannot.
boon.Steadfast Presence: Fear doesn't seem to be able to get a grip on you. You don't hide it well - you just don't really get scared and people can tell. When things go wrong, everyone in the room turns to you. Your stoicism in the face of adversity steadies those around you.
boon.Trained by a Master: Somebody who was genuinely the best taught you, and they didn't waste time on the flashy parts. They taught you what to do when it goes wrong. Years later, at the moment it goes wrong, you hear their voice and your hands are already doing it.
boon.Unshakeable Alibi: You always have a story - a time, a place, a reason and enough inane details that nobody wants to hear them. It's not a lie - you were really there.
boon.Unstoppable: What should leave you unconscious and bleeding on the floor, simply doesn't. You can still die, you are just conscious for it.
boon.Weathered: You never understood why people are constantly worried about the weather. You simply don't make it an issue. Heat that melts the dog, cold that drives people inside, hurricane force winds - none of it stops you. The cold never bothered you, anyway

flaw.Amnesia: There is a hole where a piece of your life used to be. You know it's there the way you know a tooth is gone - you keep checking. Sometimes something surfaces. A smell, a name, a room you have never been in. Then it's gone again.
flaw.Antagonist: Somebody out there is thinking about you right now, and they are not wishing you well. They know your name. They know where you eat lunch. You made an impression on exactly the wrong person, and they are patient.
flaw.Anxiety: Your brain runs a threat assessment every waking second and it never files a clean report. The stove. The email. The look somebody gave you four years ago. You know most of it isn't real. Knowing has never once made it stop.
flaw.Berserk: There is a switch, and you are not the one who flips it. Once it's thrown you are a passenger - swinging until there is nothing standing and nobody left to swing at. Afterward, other people tell you what you did.
flaw.Code of Conduct: You have a line. You drew it yourself, nobody else is obligated to respect it, and that is exactly why it counts. It has cost you money, opportunities and at least one friendship. You would draw it again tomorrow.
flaw.Dependent: Somebody needs you. A kid, a sibling, an old friend who never got their feet under them - whoever it is, they can't do this without you, and they don't get a vote in what you've gotten yourself into. Every plan has to include them.
flaw.Destitute: Money is something that happens to other people. You know which places let you sit for hours over one coffee, which shelter has the fewest rules, and exactly how far what's in your pocket will stretch. You are very good at arithmetic you never wanted to learn.
flaw.Directionless: North is a rumor. Everyone else seems to have a map running somewhere behind their eyes and you never got issued one. You have been lost inside a building you work in. "It's two blocks that way" means nothing to you.
flaw.Fragile: Other people get a bruise. You get a hairline fracture. Whatever everybody else's body does to absorb a hit, yours never learned. You break easily, you heal slowly, and you have built your whole life around knowing both.
flaw.Gun-Shy: The moment it kicks off, there is a gap. Everyone else is already moving and you are still catching up to the fact that this is happening. It isn't cowardice - you get there. You just get there late, and late is expensive.
flaw.Illiterate: The letters are right there and they don't come together. You have built an entire life around not needing them to - you memorize, you ask, you get somebody else to check the form. It works right up until someone hands you something and waits.
flaw.Impaired Senses: One channel is down. You have rerouted around it well enough that people forget, and you let them. It stays forgotten until somebody speaks up from your bad side, or the thing you needed to notice was over there.
flaw.Incantations: It doesn't work if you can't say it. Something out there is listening for the specific words and it is not interested in what you meant. A hand over your mouth is enough to stop you. So is a room where being heard would be a disaster.
flaw.Item of Power: What you can do isn't entirely in you. Some of it lives in an object - a ring, a coat, a beat-up guitar case - and objects get lost, stolen, confiscated and left in somebody else's car.
flaw.Lame: The distance hasn't changed. What it costs you has. Stairs are a decision. "It's not far" is something other people say. You get where you are going - you just get there later, and you pay for it that night.
flaw.Notable Appearance: People remember you. Every time, whether that's useful or not. The witness description is never vague and the bartender never has to ask twice. You have never once been "some guy" and you never will be.
flaw.Notoriety: Your name gets to the room before you do, and it has already said something you would rather it hadn't. Some of what they heard is true. The rest has been improved in the retelling, and nobody is interested in your correction.
flaw.Overconfident: You have been right enough times to stop checking. That worked out beautifully, right up until the day it didn't, and you are not convinced that day counts. You will take the odds. You always take the odds.
flaw.Pariah: There is a category people drop you into on sight and nothing you do gets you out of it. Being polite doesn't. Being useful doesn't. Being right definitely doesn't. You stopped waiting for the room to come around a long time ago.
flaw.Reliance: There is something you need, and the needing keeps its own schedule. It doesn't care what else is happening. It doesn't negotiate, it doesn't wait for a good moment, and it always collects.
flaw.Ritual Required: It answers. It just doesn't answer immediately. There is a procedure - words, motions, something burned, something owed - and it takes as long as it takes. Nobody has ever kicked in a door at a convenient moment.
flaw.Secret: One fact. That is all it is. One fact, and an entire life built carefully around it staying where it is. You have gotten good at steering a conversation. You have gotten better at leaving the room.
flaw.Shaken Confidence: It happened once, in front of people who mattered, and some part of you never quite stood back up. Everyone else forgot about it years ago. You did not. You feel it in the room every time something similar starts.
flaw.Short Fuse: The distance between the provocation and your response is a lot shorter than most people's. You are not proud of it. You have apologized for it. And the next time somebody says the wrong thing, you will be halfway through the response before you notice you started.
flaw.Soft-Hearted: You know what the smart move is. Everybody does. You have simply never been able to make yourself do it - not to somebody already down, already scared, already smaller than you. It has cost you, and you would do it the same way again.
flaw.Speech Impediment: The thought is clear. It is fast, it is complete, and it is exactly right. Getting it out of your mouth is the part that isn't. You have watched people decide what you were going to say and then answer that instead.

item.AI assistant earpiece: A bud that sits deep enough not to show, always listening for its name.
item.AR contact lenses: Soft lenses with the display printed into them. They need charging overnight in a case.
item.ATV / dirt bike: Knobbly tyres, long travel suspension, and no interest in roads.
item.Ablative shield harness: A harness of emitter pods that throws a shell which burns away as it is hit.
item.Action / body camera: A matchbox with a lens, clipped to a chest strap or a lapel.
item.Adrenaline shot (epi-pen): An auto-injector in a plastic tube. Blue to the sky, orange to the thigh.
item.Advanced trauma kit: A vacuum-packed roll of tourniquets, chest seals, airways and packing gauze.
item.Aerodyne (flying car): A car-sized airframe on ducted fans, with doors and a boot like anything else.
item.Amphibious conversion vehicle: A four-wheel-drive with a sealed hull, a propeller and seams that need checking.
item.Animal traps: Wire snares and a few small spring traps, rolled in canvas.
item.Anti-materiel rifle: Fifty calibre, a bipod, and a muzzle brake that hurts everyone nearby more than the shooter.
item.Antitoxin: A vial and a syringe in a cold pack, with the venom it answers written on the label.
item.Armored coat: A long wool coat with panels sewn between the lining and the shell. Heavier than it looks on the hanger.
item.Armored personnel carrier: Eight wheels, a hull, and no explaining it to anybody who sees it.
item.Armored sedan: A factory car with the doors, pillars and glass replaced. It sits low on its springs.
item.Armored suit lining: Soft panels tailored into a two-piece. Somebody was paid well to make it hang right.
item.Armored transport van: A cash-in-transit van with gun ports and a door nobody opens from outside.
item.Ascender / rappel kit: Two handled cams, a descender, slings and locking carabiners.
item.Audio sweep radio: A radio modified to sweep the band without stopping.
item.Avalanche beacon: A transceiver worn against the chest, transmitting until somebody switches it to search.
item.Ballistic briefcase: Leather over rated panels. One tug on the handle and it drops open into a shield as long as your torso.
item.Ballistic cap insert: A curved plate of hard fiber cut to sit inside an ordinary baseball cap.
item.Ballistic helmet: A high-cut composite shell with a four-point harness and rails nobody has used.
item.Ballistic shield: A slab of laminate with a viewport and two handles, about the size of a door panel.
item.Baseball bat: Ash or aluminium, thirty-odd inches. The aluminium ones ring when they connect.
item.Battle spear: A steel head on an ash shaft, taller than the person carrying it.
item.Bayonet: A blade built to clamp onto a rifle, used off it more often than on.
item.Bear spray: A fire-extinguisher-sized canister with a safety clip and a belt holster.
item.Bear trap: Forty pounds of sprung steel jaws on a chain and a stake.
item.Bicycle: A bike. Quiet, cheap, and it goes where cars cannot.
item.Binoculars: Roof prism, ten by forty-two, rubber armoured.
item.Bio-regeneration tank: A filled cylinder with a lid, a pump stack and a body suspended inside it.
item.Biometric scanner lock: A handheld reader with a gel pad, and a cable that goes somewhere it should not.
item.Black powder pistol: A single shot, loaded down the muzzle. Takes a minute and a steady hand.
item.Blank amulet: A flat silver disc on a cord, unmarked on both faces.
item.Blessed rounds: A box of twenty, each round blessed before it was loaded.
item.Blessed water: A vial of water out of a font, stoppered and sealed with wax. It looks like water.
item.Blinding strobe: A handheld lamp that pulses hard enough to be felt behind the eyes.
item.Blowgun: A metre of hollow tube and a tin of darts.
item.Bola: Three weights on cords, spun and let go.
item.Bolt cutters: Thirty-six inch handles and hardened jaws. Nothing subtle about carrying them.
item.Bomb disposal suit: Ninety pounds of layered aramid and plate, with a fan in the helmet and a wire to a controller.
item.Boomerang: Shaped hardwood, flat on one face. The kind that comes back is not the kind built for hunting.
item.Braindance recorder: A headset that records everything a person saw, heard and felt, for somebody else to wear.
item.Brass knuckles: Four finger holes cast in one piece. Illegal in more places than people assume.
item.Breaching kit: A hooligan bar, a hydraulic ram, cutting charges and hearing protection.
item.Brigandine: Steel plates riveted between canvas and leather. The rivet heads show in rows.
item.Bump key set: Filed-down blanks in the common profiles, and a plastic mallet to tap them.
item.Burn bag: A lined sack with a pull igniter in the seam. Everything in it goes to ash.
item.Burn gel / dressing: Sterile gel-soaked pads in foil, sized from a hand to a torso.
item.Camera jammer: A box that fills a camera’s sensor with light nobody in the room can see.
item.Cargo van: White, high roof, no windows in the back. Nobody looks at it twice.
item.Chain whip: Linked steel sections with a weight at the end, folded down to nothing in a pocket.
item.Chainmail: Riveted rings, twenty pounds of them, worn over padding because the alternative is bruising.
item.Chainmail dive suit: Stainless steel mesh from scalp to ankle, made for divers who work among sharks.
item.Chainsaw: Petrol, two-stroke, and loud enough that nothing in the building is unaware of you.
item.Charm bag: A cloth bag the size of a plum, drawstring at the neck.
item.Chemical analysis kit: Reagent bottles, a spot plate and a card of colour references.
item.Cleansing bundle: Rosemary, lavender, juniper or mugwort, dried and bound with cotton thread.
item.Cold iron nail: A hand-forged nail, black, square in section. Drawn wire will not do.
item.Cold iron rounds: A box of twenty, cast from wrought iron rather than lead. They foul a barrel.
item.Collapsible baton: Telescoping steel, twenty-one inches out, flicked open with a wrist.
item.Collapsible rifle case: A padded case that breaks down into something a tennis racket would fit in.
item.Colored contact lenses: Tinted soft lenses in a case, in three shades nobody would remark on.
item.Combat drone (rotor): A quadcopter with a weapon mount under it and armour over the motors.
item.Combat knife: Seven inches, full tang, a blood groove nobody needs.
item.Comms relay beacon: A weatherproof box the size of a brick, with a magnet on one face and a stub aerial.
item.Compact SMG: A folding stock and a thirty-round magazine in a package the size of a laptop.
item.Compact pistol: Polymer frame, short barrel, built to sit under a jacket and be forgotten about.
item.Compass: Baseplate, liquid-damped needle, a lanyard. No battery to go flat.
item.Compound bow: Cams and cables. Holds most of the draw weight for you once it is back.
item.Concealable microphone: A microphone the size of a shirt button on a hair-thin lead.
item.Concealable vest: Soft panels in a carrier that goes under a shirt. Hot, and everybody who wears one says so.
item.Concealed wrist blades: Spring blades in forearm sheaths, released by turning the wrist against a catch.
item.Consecrated iron fragment: A shard off a church bell, thumb-sized and still curved.
item.Consecrated oil: Olive oil in a small glass bottle, blessed and left to stand a week.
item.Covert GPS tracker: A puck with a magnet, a battery good for a fortnight, and no lights on it.
item.Covert plate vest: Thin rifle plates in a carrier cut to vanish under a jacket, bought from a man who does not ask what size you are.
item.Crossbow: A bow lying on its side with a trigger. Slow to load and no harder to aim than a rifle.
item.Crowbar: A yard of forged steel, flat one end, curved the other.
item.DNA-scrubbing wipes: Foil sachets of enzyme wipes that leave a surface less clean than empty.
item.Dart pistol: Compressed gas and a magazine of darts. Quiet, and obviously not a firearm up close.
item.Data cloner: A write-blocked duplicator that takes a drive image and leaves no timestamps behind.
item.Dead drop cache: A weatherproof tube and a spot nobody watches. The spot is the expensive part.
item.Defibrillator (AED): A hard case with two pads and a voice that talks you through it.
item.Deployable armor case: A hard-shell case the size of carry-on luggage that unfolds around you, plate by plate, and seals at the throat.
item.Derringer: Two barrels, palm-sized. Meant for a range where missing is not the problem.
item.Digital voice recorder: A pocket recorder with a better microphone than it needs.
item.Directional microphone: A shotgun mic in a foam windshield, on a pistol grip.
item.Disguise kit: Spirit gum, pigments, brushes, appliances and a mirror that folds flat.
item.Dowsing rods: Two brass rods bent into L shapes, held loose in the fists.
item.Drone control rig: A harness with a folding screen and two thumbsticks, worn across the chest.
item.Duct tape: A roll of it. Everybody has an opinion about which brand.
item.EMF meter: A handheld meter with a needle and five LEDs above it.
item.EMP device: A capacitor bank and a coil in a flight case. One shot, and then it is scrap too.
item.Economy sedan: Four doors, grey, ten years old. The most invisible object on this page.
item.Encrypted burner phone: A cheap handset with an encrypted messenger on it, bought for cash.
item.Encrypted comms set: Earpiece, throat mic and a belt unit. Everything on the set is paired to everything else.
item.Energy rifle: A rifle with no chamber and no brass, drawing from a cell in the stock.
item.English longbow: Six feet of yew. Pulling it properly deforms the bones of anyone who does it for years.
item.Environment-matched camo: A pattern chosen for one specific place, not a general-purpose one.
item.Estate: A house with a name rather than a number, at the end of a drive nobody turns down by accident.
item.Evil eye charm: Blue glass with a white and black eye in the middle. Sold on every market stall on the Mediterranean.
item.Face-changing prosthetics kit: Cast silicone appliances, adhesive and pigments, keyed to one specific face.
item.Facial recognition tablet: A tablet with a camera and a database on it that nobody is supposed to have.
item.Faraday sleeve: A padded pouch lined with silver mesh, with a roll-top closure.
item.Field autodoc: A case that opens into a frame over a patient, with arms that do the work themselves.
item.Field rations & water purifier: Retort pouches, a pump filter and spare cartridges.
item.Field stimulant: Ampoules in a foam block. Whatever is in them is not sold over a counter.
item.Fingerprint gloves: Thin nitrile with textured pads. Leaves marks that are nobody’s.
item.Fire axe: Red, with a pick on the back, off a wall somewhere.
item.Fire starter kit: Ferro rod, striker, waxed tinder in a tin that seals.
item.First aid kit: A zip pouch of dressings, tape, gloves and scissors.
item.Flail: A head on a chain on a handle. Goes around a guard rather than through it.
item.Flare gun: Fat-barrelled, bright orange, loaded with something meant to be seen for miles.
item.Flashbang: A perforated steel body. Light and pressure, no fragments.
item.Flex cuffs: Heavy zip ties, doubled, cut off rather than unlocked.
item.Forged badge / credentials: A badge and a card wallet, correct down to the holographic overlay.
item.Forged documents: Passport, licence and supporting paper, made by somebody who checks their own work.
item.Full tactical rig: Plate carrier, helmet, throat and groin protection. Everything, and it weighs everything.
item.Full-spectrum camera: A camera with the infrared filter taken out of it.
item.GPS jammer: A cigarette packet with an aerial, putting noise across the satellite band.
item.Gambeson: Quilted linen stuffed with tow. Worn alone it is a coat; worn under steel it is the reason the steel works.
item.Garrote: Wire between two handles, carried coiled in a pocket.
item.Gas mask / respirator: Full-face, twin filters, straps that take a minute to get right.
item.Gauntlets: Articulated plates over leather gloves, fingers and all.
item.Ghillie suit: A net oversuit hung with jute garnish, tied on in handfuls over weeks.
item.Glaive: A long single-edged blade on a shaft. Cuts at a distance most people misjudge.
item.Glow sticks: A dozen plastic tubes. Snap one and it cannot be switched off again.
item.Go-bag: A packed holdall by the door. Clothes, cash, documents, a charger and a knife.
item.Grapple gloves: Gloves with a launcher on the back of each wrist and a spool in the cuff.
item.Grappling hook: Three folding flukes on a steel eye, with fifty feet of line.
item.Grappling snare: A spring-loaded loop on a ground plate, set and covered over.
item.Graveyard dirt: A jam jar of soil taken off a grave.
item.Greaves: Shaped plates strapped over the shins.
item.Grenade launcher: Single shot, break action, a fat forty-millimetre bore and a ladder sight.
item.Gyro-stabilized superbike: A litre bike with active stabilisation. Stays upright doing things that should not.
item.Gyrojet pistol: Fires rocket rounds rather than bullets. Harmless up close and unpleasant at distance.
item.Hacking multitool: A slab of ports and adaptors with a screen on it, small enough for a jacket pocket.
item.Hag stone: A beach pebble with a hole worn through it by water. The hole has to be natural.
item.Halberd: An axe, a spike and a hook on one pole, for three different problems.
item.Hand axe: A hatchet balanced to be thrown as well as swung.
item.Hand crossbow: A crossbow cut down to one hand. The draw weight comes down with it.
item.Hand saw: A bow saw with a spare blade taped to the frame.
item.Handcuffs: Chain-linked steel, double locked with the tip of the key.
item.Handheld thermal camera: A pistol-grip camera with a small screen showing everything warm in white.
item.Hang glider / wingsuit: A wing in a bag, or a suit with webbing between the limbs. Both are one-way.
item.Harpoon gun: A barbed head on a line, fired from a stock. Built for things in water.
item.Hatchet: A camp axe. Splits kindling and is always to hand.
item.Hazmat suit: Sealed coveralls, taped cuffs, a hood and a filter. Single use if it is ever actually needed.
item.Heavy revolver: Six chambers, a barrel long enough to be a nuisance, and no jams.
item.Hidden camera: A pinhole lens built into something ordinary, with a card slot in the back of it.
item.Hidden tracker dart: A tracker in a dart body, fired from a gas launcher and sticky on impact.
item.Horse & tack: A horse, a saddle, a bridle and the knowledge of how to use all three.
item.Hot air balloon: An envelope, a basket, burners and a truck to collect you afterwards.
item.Hunting rifle: Bolt action, wooden stock, a scope somebody sighted in years ago.
item.IV kit & fluids: Bags of saline, giving sets, cannulas and a length of tape.
item.Ice axe: A steel head on a short shaft, pick one side, adze the other.
item.Incense and censer: A pierced brass bowl on three chains, and a box of cones.
item.Infrared thermometer: A pistol-grip thermometer with a laser dot on the front.
item.Intrusion deck: A purpose-built machine with its own radios and an operating system nobody sells.
item.Iron filings: A pound of iron swarf in a tin. It rusts if the lid is left off.
item.Iron handcuffs: Hand-forged cuffs, heavier than police issue, with a key that fits nothing else.
item.Iron horseshoe: A used shoe off a working horse, nail holes and all.
item.Javelin: A throwing spear, light, with the weight forward.
item.Jet pack: Two ducted fans on a frame, with a harness and about ninety seconds of fuel.
item.Kama: A short blade set at a right angle to the handle. It started as a rice knife.
item.Katana: A curved single edge, folded steel, a grip for one hand or two.
item.Kayak / canoe: A hull, a paddle and a spray deck. Portable if two people are willing.
item.Knee and elbow pads: Hard caps on neoprene sleeves, the kind a skater or a SWAT team buys in bulk.
item.Knotted cord: A yard of cord with nine knots along it.
item.Kukri: A heavy forward-angled blade. Chops out of proportion to its size.
item.Laptop / hacking rig: A heavy laptop with too many ports and a battery that has been replaced twice.
item.Laser listening device: A laser and a receiver on a tripod, aimed at a windowpane from across the street.
item.Laser rangefinder: Monocular, rubber-armoured, reads out distance in the eyepiece.
item.Leather cuirass: Hardened leather, front and back, laced at the sides.
item.Less-lethal shotgun (beanbag): A shotgun with an orange stock, so nobody loads it wrong in a hurry.
item.Light helicopter: A four-seat turbine. Needs somewhere flat and everybody knowing you have arrived.
item.Lockpick set: A leather wallet of rakes, hooks and tension wrenches.
item.Long-range parabolic dish: A metre of dish on a tripod, with a preamp and a recorder in the case.
item.Mace: A flanged steel head on a short haft. Does not care what the armour is made of.
item.Machete: Eighteen inches of soft steel. Cheap, everywhere, and sharpened on a stone.
item.Medical scanner: A handheld unit run over a patient, reading out more than a pulse.
item.Metal pipe: A length of scaffold or plumbing, picked up on the way past.
item.Mini-submarine: A two-person hull with a battery bank, viewports and eight hours of air.
item.Monofilament blade: A handle with nothing coming out of it until the light catches the line. It is all edge.
item.Monofilament garrote: The same filament between two handles, on a spool in a cigarette packet.
item.Motion sensor: A palm-sized sensor on a peel-and-stick pad, paired to a phone.
item.Motor yacht: Forty feet, twin diesels, berths for six and a tender on the back.
item.Motorcycle: Six hundred cubic centimetres of it, and it fits through traffic.
item.Motorcycle armor jacket: Textile with CE armour in the shoulders, elbows and back. Reads as a jacket because it is one.
item.Motorcycle leathers: A one-piece race suit, armor sewn in at the spine, shoulders, elbows and knees, scuffed from the last time it met the road.
item.Multitool: Pliers, blades, drivers and a file, folded into a handle.
item.Muzzleloader rifle: Powder, ball and ramrod. One shot and then a long wait.
item.Nail gun: Pneumatic, framing weight, with the safety nose removed by somebody.
item.Naloxone kit: Two doses of nasal spray in a hard case, with the instructions printed on the lid.
item.Nanite repair kit: An ampoule of grey fluid and an applicator. It works on the machine, not the pilot.
item.Net gun: A weighted net folded into four barrels, fired by compressed gas.
item.Net launcher: A weighted net in a compressed-gas launcher. Opens in the air.
item.Nice backpack: Forty litres, a proper hip belt, and a lifetime guarantee somebody will honour.
item.Night vision goggles: A head harness and two tubes. Everything through them is green and flat.
item.Night-vision drone: A quadcopter with a low-light camera under it, quiet enough to lose track of.
item.Nunchaku: Two hardwood batons on a short chain.
item.Off-road SUV: Body on frame, locking differentials, and tyres that hum on tarmac.
item.Optical camouflage cloak: A weighted cloak that shows whatever is behind it, a half-second late.
item.Oxygen tank: A small cylinder with a regulator and a mask, good for about twenty minutes.
item.Parabolic microphone: A clear plastic dish with a microphone at the focus and headphones on a lead.
item.Parachute: A ram-air canopy, harness, reserve and an automatic opener nobody argues with.
item.Paracord (100ft): A hank of 550 cord. Seven inner strands, and people use those separately.
item.Pepper spray: A keyring canister with a flip cover, a stream rather than a mist.
item.Pepper spray gel: A thicker formulation that goes where it is aimed and stays there.
item.Personal watercraft: A jet-drive ski for two, fast in a straight line and no use in a swell.
item.Pickaxe: A point one side, a chisel the other, on a hickory haft.
item.Pickup truck: A bed, a tow hitch, and a cab that seats three at a push.
item.Plate armor: Articulated steel over the whole body. Distributes its weight properly and is still exhausting.
item.Police scanner: A handheld receiver with a rubber aerial, scanning preset ranges.
item.Portable camp stove: A burner that screws onto a gas canister, and a wind shield that never quite works.
item.Portable charger / power bank: A brick of cells that will charge a phone six times over.
item.Portable jammer array: Four transmitters on stands, covering everything from a room to a street.
item.Private jet: Light twin, six seats, and a crew who have been told not to file a passenger list.
item.Prosthetic scars / tattoo kit: Silicone appliances, transfer inks and remover, in a flat tin.
item.Pump shotgun: Twelve gauge, tube magazine, the sound of the action doing half the work.
item.RF / bug detector: A wand with a meter on it, swept slowly along a wall.
item.RFID cloner: A reader and a writer in one case, with a stack of blank fobs.
item.RFID skimmer: A reader in a satchel, picking up cards through a coat at walking distance.
item.Rapier: A long narrow blade with a cage over the hand. Built entirely around the point.
item.Reactive plate vest: Tiles of explosive laminate over a steel back plate. It stops the round by throwing itself at it.
item.Recon drone: A folding quadcopter in a hard case, with a camera on a gimbal.
item.Recurve bow: Limbs curving away at the tips. Takedown, so it travels in a bag.
item.Residue sample kit: Swabs, vials, a UV lamp and a box of evidence bags.
item.Revolver rifle: A cylinder in a rifle stock. Rare, and it spits at the wrist that holds it.
item.Riot exoskeleton: A powered frame worn outside the armour, motors at the joints, a battery on the back.
item.Riot helmet: Full face, polycarbonate visor, neck guard hanging off the back.
item.Riot shield: Clear polycarbonate, body length, with a horizontal grip and a forearm cuff.
item.Ritual candles: A dozen plain candles, unscented, wicks already trimmed.
item.Ritual chalk: A box of soft white sticks. They mark anything, including things chalk should not mark.
item.Road flares: Fusees in a cardboard tube. Fifteen minutes each, and they burn in rain.
item.Rope & climbing kit: Fifty metres of dynamic rope, a harness, belay device and a rack of gear.
item.Rowan and red thread: Two rowan twigs bound into a cross with red wool.
item.Rubber bullet launcher: A break-action launcher with a wide bore and a padded stock.
item.Rue sachet: Dried rue in a linen bag, stitched shut.
item.SAM splint: A rolled aluminium and foam strip, bent to shape around a limb.
item.Safe house (urban): A flat on a middle floor, rented under a company, with the bills paid by standing order.
item.Safecracking kit: An autodialler, a borescope, a magnetic mount and a great deal of patience.
item.Sai: A blunt spike with two side prongs, carried in pairs. Built to trap a blade.
item.Salt circle kit: A tin holding measured salt, a length of cord and a stick of chalk.
item.Salt, canister: A cardboard canister of coarse salt. The cheap kind, off a supermarket shelf.
item.Salt-loaded shells: Ten shotgun shells packed with rock salt in place of shot.
item.Sap: Lead shot in a leather pouch, flat enough for a back pocket.
item.Satellite phone: A handset with a thick hinged aerial, and it needs open sky to be any use at all.
item.Satellite uplink: A folding dish in a hard case, with a terminal that takes ten minutes to find the sky.
item.Sawed-off shotgun: Both barrels cut back to nothing. Fits under a coat and spreads immediately.
item.Sealed environment armor: Hard shell, sealed seams, its own air on the back and a faceplate that fogs at the edges.
item.Security drone (tracked): Waist-high, tracked, armoured, with a sensor mast and a speaker.
item.Sedative dart: A single dart with a pressurised chamber behind the needle.
item.Service pistol: Full-size automatic, fifteen rounds, what a duty holster is shaped for.
item.Sewing / repair kit: Needles, waxed thread, patches and a few buttons in a tobacco tin.
item.Shear-thickening suit: A suit of ordinary-looking cloth soaked in a fluid that goes hard as stone the instant anything hits it.
item.Shock baton: A baton with contacts at the tip and a trigger under the thumb.
item.Shock dart gun: A blocky handgun firing two barbs on wires, with a cartridge in the nose.
item.Short sword: Two feet of straight double edge. Indoors it beats anything longer.
item.Signal jammer: A handheld unit with three stubby aerials and a bank of switches.
item.Signal triangulator: Three receivers and a tablet, drawing a shrinking circle around a transmitter.
item.Silver buckshot: Ten shells loaded with cast silver balls.
item.Silver dust: A vial of silver ground finer than flour.
item.Silver rounds: A box of twenty, cast solid rather than plated.
item.Skateboard / scooter: Board or kick scooter. Goes under an arm at the door.
item.Sled / dog sled: A basket sled, a gangline and a team who know the route better than you do.
item.Sledgehammer: Ten pounds on a hickory handle. Meant for masonry.
item.Sling: A leather cradle and two cords. Older than everything else on this page.
item.Small fixed-wing aircraft: Four seats, one engine, and a strip short enough to be unofficial.
item.Smart glasses: Ordinary frames with a projector in one arm and a camera in the other.
item.Smartgun link kit: A rail sensor, a wire, and a reticle that goes wherever the muzzle is actually pointed.
item.Smartphone: A phone. Everybody has one and everybody’s is slightly out of date.
item.Smoke grenade: A canister that burns rather than bursts, throwing smoke for a minute.
item.Snake bite kit: A suction pump, bandages and instructions most people have not read.
item.Snowshoes: Aluminium frames with decking and a ratchet binding.
item.Snub-nose revolver: Five rounds, two-inch barrel, no hammer spur to catch on a pocket.
item.Solar charger: A folding panel that straps to a pack, with a regulator and two ports.
item.Sonic deterrent device: A dish on a handle, projecting a tone in a cone in front of it.
item.Speargun: Rubber bands and a steel shaft. Works properly only underwater.
item.Speedboat: An open hull with far too much outboard on the back of it.
item.Spy pen camera: A pen that writes, with a lens above the clip.
item.Squad automatic weapon: Belt-fed, bipod, a spare barrel in a bag because you will need it.
item.Stab vest: Layered mail and laminate. Built for blades, and honest about it.
item.Stimulant patch: An adhesive patch that goes on the neck and works through the skin.
item.Straw water filter: A hollow-fibre tube you drink through directly.
item.Stun gun: Two contacts and a trigger. It has to be touching to do anything.
item.Supercar: Mid-engined, carbon, and every camera on the route will remember it.
item.Surgical kit: A sterile roll of scalpels, forceps, clamps, needles and suture.
item.Surgical pod: An enclosed table with arms above it, which does not need anybody in the room.
item.Surveillance microdrone: Insect-sized. Flies in through the gap a window was left open and sends back what it sees.
item.Switchblade: Four inches, spring-loaded, opens with a thumb.
item.Tablet / e-reader: A tablet in a knocked-about case, loaded with more than anybody could read.
item.Tactical carbine: Short-barrelled semi-auto, adjustable stock, rails for whatever you bolt to it.
item.Tactical flashlight: Anodised aluminium, a tail switch, and bright enough to be an argument.
item.Tactical vest: A plate carrier with hard plates front and back and pouches across the front.
item.Tear gas grenade: A burning canister, hot enough that picking it up to throw back costs something.
item.Technical scanner: A handheld unit with a probe on a coiled lead and a screen that is mostly menus.
item.Tent: Two-person, three-season, and the poles are colour-coded for a reason.
item.Tent & sleeping gear: The tent, a bag rated lower than you need, and a mat that will deflate by morning.
item.Thermal drone: A quadcopter carrying a thermal camera instead of an ordinary one.
item.Thermal imaging scope: A scope that clips ahead of an existing optic, showing heat rather than light.
item.Thermite charge: A shaped canister with an igniter. Burns through what it is sat on.
item.Threshold ward kit: A canvas roll holding chalk, salt, iron filings and cord.
item.Throwing knife: No edge worth speaking of. All of it is balance.
item.Tonfa: A baton with a side handle. Guards the forearm as well as it strikes.
item.Tourniquet: A windlass on a webbing strap, one-handed by design.
item.Trail camera: A camouflaged box strapped to a tree, motion-triggered, with infrared for night.
item.Tranquilizer rifle: A single dart on compressed gas. The dose is a guess and the wait is worse.
item.Trauma patch: A sealed dressing with a clotting agent already in the gauze.
item.Trauma shears: Angled shears that cut a boot off without touching what is inside it.
item.Trench knife: A blade with knuckles built into the grip. Exactly as old as the name suggests.
item.Turnout gear: Firefighter's bunker gear: coat, trousers, hood and helmet, heavy, reflective, and rated to walk into a fire.
item.Two-handed sword: Five feet of it, and a grip long enough to need both hands honestly.
item.Two-way radio: A pair of handhelds off a shelf. Anybody with the same set can hear you.
item.UV flashlight: A torch throwing almost nothing visible. Things on a floor light up under it.
item.Underground facility: Excavated, powered, and on no plan ever filed with the city.
item.Uniform disguise: Somebody’s actual work clothes, with the right boots and a laminated card.
item.Utility trailer: A flatbed on a tow ball, with a ramp and a tarpaulin.
item.Voice changer: An inline unit between a handset and an earpiece, with a dial.
item.War axe: A bearded head on a two-foot haft. The beard is for pulling shields down.
item.War fan: Steel ribs in a folding fan. Closed it is a baton, open it is a guard.
item.Warding paint: A rattle can, or a brush and a tin. Both work.
item.Warhammer: A hammer face one side, a spike the other, on a long haft.
item.Water desalinator: A hand-pumped reverse osmosis unit. Slow, and heavier than the brochure said.
item.Water purification tablets: A strip of foil-wrapped tablets. Thirty minutes and it tastes of a swimming pool.
item.Welding torch: Oxy-acetylene on a trolley, with a striker on a chain.
item.Whip: Twelve feet of plaited leather. Everything it does is at the tip.
item.Wig & makeup kit: Two wigs on blocks, pins, and a case of everything to go with them.
item.Wire ascent rig: A powered ascender that climbs a fixed line faster than a person can.
item.Wiretap kit: Alligator clips, a recorder and a lineman’s handset in a battered bag.
item.Witch bottle: A glass bottle of pins, nail clippings and worse, sealed with wax.

resource.Base: Somewhere that is yours. A door you control, a lock you picked out, and nobody's name on the lease that you didn't want there. It might be a room over a garage or a whole floor nobody else visits. Either way, you can shut the door and breathe.
resource.Black Market Access: There is a version of every store that doesn't ask, doesn't record and doesn't remember you came in. A guy with a van. A back room behind a laundromat. A number you text one word to. You know where those are.
resource.Contacts: You don't know the answer. You know four people, and one of them does. A cop who owes you. A nurse who works nights. Somebody's cousin at the airport. It isn't what you know - it's who picks up when you call.
resource.Corporate Backing: Something enormous and entirely legal has decided you are useful. It moves slowly, it moves in writing, and once it moves it is very hard to stop. There is a budget code with your name on it and a lawyer who already knows who you are.
resource.Debts Owed: People owe you. Not favors, exactly - the other kind. The kind nobody gets out of by saying they're busy. You don't bring it up often. You have never needed to. They remember.
resource.Fame: People know your face. The room changes when you walk into it, and not always in the direction you would like. Strangers are friendly, or they aren't, and either way they decided something about you before you opened your mouth.
resource.Followers: You have people who will actually go when you say go. Not fans. Not friends who would think about it and get back to you. People who turn up with a van at four in the morning and ask what it's for later.
resource.Fringe Benefit: A card, a title, a laminated badge, a line on a form. Most people don't know that door is a door. You have the thing that opens it, and nobody at the desk is going to argue with you about it.
resource.Guild Standing: Inside one trade, your name means something specific. You don't have to be in the room for it to mean it. People who have never met you know where you rank and behave accordingly.
resource.Informant Network: A lot of people see a lot of small things. Doormen, dishwashers, the guy running the newsstand, the kid who is always outside. Not one of them knows anything important. All of them tell you what they saw.
resource.Legal Counsel: Somebody whose entire job is standing between you and the consequences, and who is very good at it. They answer at two in the morning. They don't ask what you did. They ask what you said, and to whom.
resource.Media Contact: A story runs, or it doesn't. Somebody decides which, and you know them well enough to call. What ends up in the paper is not the same thing as what happened, and you have a hand in the difference.
resource.Medical Access: Care that happens quietly and competently, with nobody filling out the form asking how this occurred. A clinic that keeps odd hours. A surgeon who owes somebody. You get stitched up and you go home.
resource.Occult Library: Shelves of things most people would find unbearably dull and a few people would burn the building down to reach. Some of it is photocopied. Some of it should never have been photocopied. You know where every piece of it is.
resource.Safehouse Network: Somewhere to go that isn't home, in more than one direction, already stocked. Cash, a change of clothes, a phone nobody has the number for. You have never needed all of them at once. You keep them all anyway.
resource.Sanctuary Standing: There is one patch of ground where nothing touches you, and everybody standing on it knows why. Get through that door and whatever is chasing you has to stop and think it over.
resource.Signature Possession: One object. Yours specifically, known to be yours, and worth something to somebody other than you. A car, a watch, an instrument, a gun with a history. People recognize it before they recognize you.
resource.Spiritual Standing: Within one faith, your word carries weight that has nothing to do with what you can prove. People listen because of where you stand, not because of the argument you made. That cuts both ways and you know it.
resource.System Access: Doors that aren't doors, opened with credentials that are genuinely yours. You aren't breaking in. You are logging in, and the log says you were supposed to be there.
resource.Territory: Actual ground that answers to you. Not owned - owned is a different thing, and much easier. Nobody deals on this block, drinks in this bar or parks on this street without it getting back to you.
resource.Underworld Reputation: In the parts of town with no signage, people have heard of you, and they have heard something specific. You never have to introduce yourself. You do occasionally have to correct the story.
resource.Vehicle: It gets you there, and people notice which one it is. That's the trade. Everybody remembers the car, which is wonderful right up until somebody is describing it to a police sketch artist.
resource.Wealth: Money you can actually reach, which is a different thing from money you technically have. Net worth is a number on paper. This is what's in the account on a Tuesday, and it's the only one that matters when you need something today.
